Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of injury sustained by the petitioner in MVC.No.5302/2022 and damages caused to the Scooter bearing No.KA-02-HH-5508 of the petitioner in MVC.No.5303/2022 in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. Since these two cases are arising out of one Shwetha A.K vs Gayathri Tiles Pvt Ltd on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110020742/

M.V.C.No.5303/2022 clubbed with original M.V.C.No.5302/2022 and common evidence came to be recorded in the said case.
These two cases are proceeded for disposal by way of common Judgment.

03. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
 That on 18.07.2022 at about 9.00 a.m, the petitioner in MVC.No.5302/2022 was riding the Scooter bearing No.KA-02-HH-5508 which belongs to petitioner in MVC.No.5303/2022), on NH-4 Tumkur Road, near 8th Mile Junction, since there was green signal riding towards Nelamangala on NH-4 Service Road, while so proceeding near Bhavani Timbers, at that time, driver of Container Lorry bearing No.
KA-01-AM-7797 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly steered towards his left side and dashed against the petitioner's scooter and caused the accident.
As a result of which she fell down and sustained grievous injuries and her Scooter was also badly damaged.

C/w M.V.C.No.5303/2022  Immediately after the accident the petitioner in MVC.No.5302/2022 was shifted to Prakriya Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery and she has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance,
nourishment and other incidental charges.

It is contended that prior to the accident she was hale and healthy, aged about 41 years and working in a Private Company and was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m and contributing the same to the welfare of her family.

Due to accidental injuries she is suffering from pain,
mental shock and she could not able to do her day to day activities as earlier.
The petitioner in MVC.No.5303/2022 was the RC owner of the Scooter bearing No.KA-02/HH-5508.
After the accident the petitioner got shifted the said Scooter to garage and spent more than Rs.20,000/- towards repair of Scooter.

During repair period he used hire Shwetha A.K vs Gayathri Tiles Pvt Ltd on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110020742/
3 vehicle for his business and other purpose, for which he spent huge amount and due to damages caused to his vehicle he has suffered mental shock and agony.
 The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Container Lorry  (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.5302/2022  C/w M.V.C.No.5303/2022 and in this regard the Peenya Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of the offending container lorry.

05. The respondent No.1 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioners, negligence on the part of the driver of container lorry, treatment taken by the petitioner and damages caused to the Scooter, expenses incurred by the petitioners towards treatment and damages and admits that this respondent is the RC owner of the Container Lorry and the same was insured with respondent No.2.

If the court comes to the conclusion that the petitioners are entitled for the compensation,
then the respondent No.2 is liable to pay  (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.5302/2022  C/w M.V.C.No.5303/2022 compensation.

The compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive and hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings and documents available on record, this tribunal framed the following:-
 ISSUES IN MVC No.5302/2022  01.

Whether the petitioner proves that  she has sustained grievous injuries in the  accident occurred on 18.07.2022 at about  (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.5302/2022  C/w M.V.C.No.5303/2022  09.00 a.m, near Bhavani Timbers, NH4  Service Road, Bengaluru, due to rash and  negligent act of the driving of the Lorry  bearing registration No.KA-01-AM-7797 by  its driver as alleged in the petition?
 02.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for  compensation?

If, so, to what amount and  from whom?
 03.
What Order or Award?
ISSUES IN MVC No.5303/2022  01.

Whether the petitioner proves that  his Scooter bearing registration No.
 KA-02-HH-5508 has sustained damages in  the accident occurred on 18.07.2022 at  about 09.00 a.m, near Bhavani Timbers,
 NH4 Service Road, Bengaluru, due to rash  and negligent act of the driving of the  Lorry bearing registration No.
 KA-01-AM-7797 by its driver as alleged in  the petition?
 02.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for  compensation?

If so, to what amount and  from whom?
 03.
What Order or Award?

12. Issue No.1 in both cases:-

The petitioner as well as petitioner No.1 respectively in both cases got herself examined as PW.1 and 2 and she has given evidence in the form of the affidavit and she has reiterated the petitions averments therein.

13. Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.5302/2022:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

Petitioner in her evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 41 years and working in a Private Company and was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance,

Due to accidental injuries, she is unable to do her work and sustained loss of income and suffering from permanent disability.

According to which, the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 13.09.1981.
The alleged accident occurred on 18.07.2022.
Therefore, it appears that at the time of accident the age of petitioner is 41 years.

Accordingly,
this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 41 years as on the date of accident.
15. As per Ex.P.12 Wound certificate the petitioner has sustained only one grievous injury.
As per Ex.P.20 and 26 Discharge summaries the petitioner was treated as inpatient for 6 days.

Further,
in this case the petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated her and has not produced any disability certificate to show that she has sustained any physical or functional disability which is come in the way of her day to day life.
Further, the Medical expenses incurred by the petitioner has been reimbursed by the Oriental Insurance Company as admitted by PW.1 in her cross-examination.

Absolutely, there is no evidence on  (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.5302/2022  C/w M.V.C.No.5303/2022 record to show that petitioner sustained any physical or functional disability and no evidence on record to show her age, avocation and income.

There is no evidence on record to show that petitioner sustained loss of future income and loss of income during laid up period and also there is no evidence on record to show that petitioner requires further treatment.

Therefore,
under the facts and circumstances of the case, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.60,000/-.

16 . Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner in M.V.C.No.5302/2022 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.60,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

Ltd., V/s Geeta Devi and others, wherein it is held that  Once seemingly valid driving licence is produced by person employed to drive a vehicle, unless such licence is demonstrably fake on face of it, inquiry by employer is not expected, burden is upon Insurance Company to prove that there was failure on the part of vehicle owner in carrying out due diligence, no evidence was placed on record whereby inference could  (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.5302/2022  C/w M.V.C.No.5303/2022 be drawn that deceased vehicle owner ought to have verified driving licence of driver, it was for Insurance Company to prove willful breach on part of vehicle owner, as no such exercise was undertaken, Insurance Company had no right to recover compensation amount from owner of vehicle.

sentences.text: The petition filed by the petitioners in M.V.C. No.5302/2022 and M.V.C.No.5303/2022 U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 are partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner in M.V.C.No.5302/2022 is entitled for compensation of Rs.60,000/- (Rupees Sixty thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment directly to her account by obtaining her bank account details.

The petitioners No.1 to 3 in M.V.C. No.5303/2022 are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,850/- (Rupees Twenty five thousand eight hundred and fifty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The petitioner No.1 being the wife and petitioners No.2 and 3 being minor daughters of the deceased petitioner
were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 70-15-15, in the award amount together with interest.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of petitioner No.1 through E-payment directly to her account by obtaining her bank account details.

Since the petitioners No.2 and 3 are minors, on deposit of the award amount with interest, the entire share amount of the petitioners No.2 and 3 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Schedule Bank till they attains age of majority in the name of their guardian with a liberty to draw accrued interest by their guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor petitioners No.2 and 3.
(SCCH-3) 22 M.V.C.No.5302/2022 C/w M.V.C.No.5303/2022 The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amounts with interest within two months from the date of these Judgments in both cases.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- in each case.
Keep the original Judgment and award in MVC No.5302/2022 and copy of the same in MVC No.5303/2022.
Draw award accordingly.

were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 70-15-15, in the award amount together with interest.
On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of petitioner No.1 through E-payment directly to her account by obtaining her bank account details.
Since the petitioners No.2 and 3 are minors, on deposit of the award amount with interest, the entire share amount of the petitioners No.2 and 3 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Schedule Bank till they attains age of majority in the name of their guardian with a liberty to draw accrued interest by their guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor petitioners No.2 and 3.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- in each case.
